title.narrative: UNDP 2021-2023 Stöd till reform av valssystem och processer
UNDP 2021-2023 Support to reform of election systems and processes

description.narrative:
By the end of the intervention, it is expected to ensure national ownership in terms of organization and the management of the electoral process.
This will be done through a strong coordination of support to the electoral cycle from partners for 1) the inclusive implementation of political and institutional reforms through the adoption of texts (new electoral law, new Constitution, new administrative and territorial mapping); 2) the organization of free, inclusive, transparent and peaceful elections in line with international standards and regional instruments governing electoral processes and integrating gender equity and respect for human rights and 3) the institutional capacity building for the management of the electoral cycle in the light of strengthening democratic governance.
The achievement of the three dimensions mentioned above is a long-term process because the conduct of an election involves a sequence of events and the engagement of several actors. The entities of the Electoral Management Body (EMB) are the main beneficiaries of the support. They will receive specific trainings to improve the election result management system including the process of counting, tabulating, aggregating and announcing the results of the election.
In addition to the EMB, direct beneficiaries will include civil society organizations, political parties and the media. Adequately-funded civil society and media organizations will play a wider role in the area of civic and voter education. Youth, women, refugees and internally displaced people also stand to benefit, and support to a more inclusive process is intended bring them into the electoral process. Finally, support to conflict management and dispute resolution aims to reduce election-related violence which often affects some of the poorest and most marginalized groups.
Sida assesses that the project is supposed to promote social equality, political inclusion and minimize electoral conflicts and build trust among the various actors targeted. In addition, the project will contribute to the stabilization and the consolidation of the peace process as elections are an important part of it.
In sum, there were three main goals of the intervention.
Specific objective 1: Support the constitutional, electoral and institutional reform process to ensure that it incorporates the expectations of the population, including vulnerable groups, women, youth and minorities;
Specific objective 2: To contribute to the organization of peaceful, inclusive, transparent, credible electoral and referendum consultations at the end of the transition;
Specific objective 3: To strengthen the short-, medium- and long-term capacities of the current institutions involved in the political and electoral processes and those resulting from the reforms with a view to making them more effective, operational, credible and worthy of the trust of the majority of Malian actors and populations.
Three axes of operationalization:
- The first axe concerns support to the reform process of national actors in the pre-electoral phase (the inclusive implementation of political and institutional reforms through the adoption of texts (new electoral law, new Constitution, new administrative and territorial mapping).
- The second axe concerns support to the organisation of the before mentioned elections (referendum and general elections).
- The third axe of intervention concerns the post-transitional phase in support of democratic governance of the institutions (the institutional capacity building for the management of the electoral cycle in the light of strengthening democratic governance).

UNDP-Mali har den maliska övergångsregeringens formella uppdrag att stödja övergången till ett demokratiskt styrelseskick, att bidra till reformer vad gäller valprocesser och stödja organisering av allmänna val.
UNDP-Mali, i samarbete med MINUSMA och UN-Women har inkommit med en ansökan om stöd till dessa två processer med en total budget om ca 55 miljoner USD mellan 1 juli 2021-31 december 2023. Omkring 46 procent av insatsen är finansierad av bland annat Kanada, EU, Norge, Spanien utöver Sverige. UNDP-Mali för diskussioner med andra länder som är intresserade att bidra.
UNDP-Mali är en nyckelaktör vad gäller valprocesser i Mali och har varit delaktig i dessa sedan Mali övergick till demokratiska val 1992. På FN:s Generalsekreterares uppdrag genomfördes en så kallad Needs Assessment Mission (NAM) vad gäller FN:s möjligheter att stödja kommande val i Mali. Rapporten rekommenderade ett nytt projekt under UNDP-Malis ledning för att stödja reformprocesser och organiserandet av allmänna val. Vidare rekommenderades upprättandet av en så kallad "basket fund" i syfte att underlätta UNDP:s koordinerande roll av det internationella samfundets bidrag samt att säkerställa att stödet blir sammanhållet och relevant. Insatsen omfattar även aktiviteter som ska genomföras av International IDEA (max fem miljoner SEK) som inom ramen för UNDP-Malis uppdrag ska stödja reformarbetet vad gäller konstitution och valprocesser.
Förändringsteorin som ligger till grund för UNDP:s valprogram är följande: Om de politiska förväntningar vad gäller politisk och institutionell reform infrias och om det maliska samhället deltar i ökad omfattning i valen och får ökat förtroende för de valförättande institutionerna och om de politiska aktörerna kan lösa sina politiska konflikter så kommer Mali träda in i en fas med demokratisk samhällsstyrning.
UNDP har två resultatområden. Det ena handlar om teknisk, logistisk och finansiellt stöd till övergångsregeringen att förbereda för val. Förväntade resultat är konstitutionell översyn och skapandet av nya val distrikt.
Det andra resultatområdet är praktiskt stöd till organiseringen och genomförande av val. Förväntade resultat av dessa aktiviteter är bland annat färdigställande av vallistor, utbildning av valarbetare, planering av val, stöd till inkludering av kvinnor i valen, uppsökande av väljare och förebyggande av konflikter relaterade till val.

UNDP-Mali has the Malian transitional government's formal request to support the transition to a democratic governance, to contribute to electoral reform and support the organisation of general elections.
In collaboration with MINUSMA and UN Women, UNDP-Mali has applied for funding to support these two processes with a total budget of 55 million USD to be carried out between July 1, 2021 to December 31, 2023. Around 46 percent of the intervention is financed by Canada, EU, Norway, Spain in addition to Sweden. UNDP-Mali is in discussion with other countries that are interested in contributing.
UNDP-Mali is a key actor with regards to elections in Mali and has been involved in organizing elections since Mali transitioned to democratic elections in 1992. At the request of the Secretary General of the UN, a Needs Assessment Mission (NAM) has been carried Spring 2021 regarding the possibilities of UN to support elections in Mali. The final report recommended a renewed support to UNDP-Mali to support electoral reform processes and the organizing of elections. In addition, the report recommends the set-up of a basket fund mechanism so to facilitate the coordinating role of UNDP-Mali, in addition to ensure the coherency and relevance of the support of the international community. The contribution includes a niched support to International IDEA (five million SEK) in the domain of constitutional and electoral reform.
The theory of change that underlies the proposed program is as follows: If the political expectations on political and institutional reform are met and if the Malian society trust the electoral institutions to an increasing extent and participates in the elections and if the political actors can solve their political conflicts then Mali will evolve in a phase of democratic governance.
UNDP-Mali has two result areas. The first is technical, logistical and financial support to the transitional government to prepare for elections. The expected results are constitutional oversight and the creation of new election districts.
The other result area is practical support to the organisation and implementation of elections. The expected results of these activities are among others: the completion of electoral lists, training of election workers, planning of elections, support to the inclusion of women in the elections, voter outreach and election related conflict prevention and mitigation.

Despite the political instability and security context, UNDP has implemented many activities including communication and public awareness-raising for more inclusive elections, support to the the Electoral Management Body "Autorité Indépendante de Gestion des Elections (AIGE); Ministry of territorial administration and decentralization and mobilizing civil society organizations for greater participation.
The following results have been achieved:
• UNDP has mobilized funds from 8 donors/funder and coordinated them to support transparent, free and fair electoral processes.
• A new Electoral Law has been adopted and an Electoral Management Body called "Autorité Indépendante de Gestion des Elections (AIGE) has been created.
• Six laws relating to administrative and territorial reorganization have been adopted on March 2023.
• The technical and operational capacities of the main electoral management bodies (AIGE, MATD, CCM) have been strengthened and they have organized on June 18, 2023 the refendum in a professional way according to international standards.
• Electoral advisors have been deployed and stationed in the 20 regional government offices and supported local commissions in charge of centralizing electoral operations.
• Civil society organizations, in particular women's and youth organisations, have been selected and awarded funds to implement communication and public awareness raising activities about elections at regional and local levels. This has been achieved through comprehensive measures, including capacity building of 45 leaders of 15 civil society organisations, exchange and consultations with 350 women leaders and 350 young leaders of political parties, complemented by many additional capacity building and awareness raising campaigns for students, market actors and others, and the distribution of information material to some to some 401,000 Malians across the country.
• Journalists have been trained on how to make an impartial and nonviolent media covering of elections, a Media and Electoral Information Centre was establihed and made operational and serveral measures to mitigate disinformation were taken together with media actors.
• As a result of these and other measures the Malian populations have been widely sensitized on the necessity of the electoral and NINA card (national identification number), how to vote and why to vote through various means of communication.
• UN systems support to elections have been evaluated to capitalize and learn lessons from the 2023 referendum and prepare for the general elections.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
